## 1. Purpose

This procedure describes the operation and care of vortex mixers used
in the EA Program laboratory. Vortex mixers produce a rapid orbital
or oscillating motion that creates a vortex inside a tube or small
container, providing fast and thorough mixing of liquids, suspensions,
and reagents. They are used routinely in DNA extraction
([SOP-L700](SOP-L700-dna-extraction.qmd)), Qubit sample preparation
([SOP-L213](SOP-L213-qubit-fluorometer.qmd)), chemical extractions,
and general reagent mixing.


## 2. Scope

- **Applies to:** All vortex mixers in the EA Program laboratory,
  including the Fisher Scientific vortex mixers (SGM 134, qty 3) and
  the Vortex-Genie 2 (SGM 133)
- **Does not apply to:** Orbital shakers (for extended, gentle
  agitation of multiple samples); magnetic stir plates; sonicators
  (see [SOP-L115](SOP-L115-sonicator.qmd))
- **Location:** SGM 133 and SGM 134


## 3. Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                              |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------|
| Lab PI            | Approve SOP                                 |
| Lab Manager       | Maintain equipment, replace cup attachments |
| Trained Personnel | Operate the vortex mixer per this SOP       |
| New Students      | Complete training before independent use    |


## 4. Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Aerosol generation:** Vortexing uncapped or loosely capped tubes
  can spray liquid and generate aerosols. Always cap tubes securely
  before vortexing. If the sample contains hazardous biological or
  chemical material, vortex inside a fume hood or biological safety
  cabinet.
- **Tube ejection:** At high speed, improperly held tubes can slip
  from the cup head and be thrown from the mixer. Hold tubes firmly
  against the cup or use the hands-free cup attachment.
- **Breakage:** Thin-walled glass tubes may shatter under vigorous
  vortexing. Use polypropylene or thick-walled borosilicate tubes
  whenever possible.
- **Entanglement:** Keep hands, hair, jewelry, and loose clothing
  away from the spinning cup head.
- **Electrical:** Do not operate the mixer with a damaged power cord
  or loose components. Inspect the cord before use; report damage to
  the lab manager.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Safety glasses
- [ ] Nitrile gloves (standard lab PPE)
- [ ] Lab coat


## 5. Equipment

| Item                                  | Location  | Notes                          |
|:--------------------------------------|:----------|:-------------------------------|
| Fisher Scientific vortex mixer        | SGM 134   | Qty 3; touch or continuous mode |
| Vortex-Genie 2 (Scientific Industries) | SGM 133  | Variable speed; touch or continuous mode |

## 6. Procedure

### 6.1 Pre-Use Inspection

1. Verify the vortex mixer is clean and free from visible damage
2. Ensure the power cord is intact and properly connected
3. Check that the rubber cup head or attachment is securely installed
   and not cracked or deformed

### 6.2 Setup

1. Verify that the vortex mixer is on a stable, flat bench surface
   and that the rubber feet are intact (prevents the unit from
   walking during operation)
2. Confirm that the appropriate head is installed:
   - **Cup head:** for individual tubes (microcentrifuge tubes,
     15 mL and 50 mL centrifuge tubes, glass test tubes)
   - **Platform head:** for microplates or tube racks (if available)
3. Set the speed dial to the desired setting. For most routine mixing,
   a medium speed (setting 5--7 on the Vortex-Genie 2 dial) is
   sufficient. Use lower speeds for gentle mixing and higher speeds
   for vigorous vortexing (e.g., bead disruption steps in DNA
   extraction).

### 6.3 Operation -- Touch Mode

Touch mode is the default for most applications. The mixer runs only
while the tube is pressed against the cup head.

1. Cap the tube securely
2. Hold the tube at a slight angle (approximately 15--30 degrees from
   vertical) and press the bottom of the tube firmly into the center
   of the cup head
3. The motor engages automatically. A visible vortex should form in
   the liquid.
4. Vortex for the duration specified in the analytical SOP (typically
   2--5 seconds for brief mixing, 10--30 seconds for thorough
   resuspension)
5. Release the tube from the cup to stop

### 6.4 Operation -- Continuous Mode

Use continuous mode for hands-free operation or when extended vortexing
is required.

1. Switch the mode selector to **Continuous** (or **On**)
2. Adjust the speed dial to the desired setting
3. Place the capped tube in the cup head or in a tube holder secured
   to the platform head
4. The motor runs continuously at the set speed
5. After the prescribed duration, switch back to **Touch** mode or
   turn off the unit
6. Remove the tube

### 6.5 Vortexing Multiple Tubes

For rapid sequential vortexing of many tubes (e.g., a rack of Qubit
assay tubes):

1. Set the mixer to touch mode at the desired speed
2. Work through the rack systematically, pressing each tube against
   the cup for 2--3 seconds
3. Return each tube to the rack before picking up the next

For simultaneous vortexing of a plate or rack, attach the platform
head and secure the plate or rack with the provided clamp or tape. Run
in continuous mode for the prescribed duration.

### 6.6 Special Applications

| Application                   | Speed Setting | Duration  | Notes                          |
|:------------------------------|:--------------|:----------|:-------------------------------|
| Brief reagent mixing          | Medium (5--7) | 2--5 s    | Touch mode; just to mix        |
| Qubit assay tube mixing (L213) | Medium (5--7) | 2--3 s   | Brief vortex after adding sample to working solution |
| DNA extraction bead disruption (L700) | Maximum (10) | Per kit protocol (often 10 min on adapter) | Use continuous mode with horizontal adapter if available |
| Resuspending pellets after centrifugation | High (8--10) | 10--30 s | Until pellet is fully resuspended |
| Mixing soil extracts (L403, L409) | Medium (5--7) | 5--10 s | Ensure homogeneous suspension before filtering |


## 7. Maintenance

| Task                                  | Frequency              |
|:--------------------------------------|:-----------------------|
| Wipe the cup head and body with 70% ethanol | After each use session |
| For eDNA/PCR work: wipe with 10% bleach, then ethanol | After each use session |
| Check rubber feet for wear            | Monthly                |
| Inspect cup head for cracks or deformation | Monthly           |
| Replace cup head                      | When cracked or deformed |

::: {.callout-note}
If liquid spills into the cup head or body of the mixer, unplug the
unit immediately, wipe up the spill, and allow to dry completely before
re-use. Liquid inside the motor housing can cause electrical failure.
:::


## 8. Waste Disposal

No waste is generated by the vortex mixer itself. Dispose of sample
waste per the relevant analytical SOP and
[SOP-L006 Waste Disposal](SOP-L006-waste-disposal.qmd).

## 11. Training Record

Before using the vortex mixer independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP in full
2. Demonstrate proper tube holding technique in touch mode (cap
   secured, slight angle, firm contact with cup)
3. Demonstrate switching between touch and continuous mode
4. Be signed off by the PI or lab manager


## Appendix A: Troubleshooting {.appendix}

| Symptom                        | Probable Cause                 | Corrective Action                          |
|:-------------------------------|:-------------------------------|:-------------------------------------------|
| Mixer does not start           | Power disconnected or cord damaged | Check power supply; inspect cord; try another outlet |
| Excessive vibration or walking | Unit on uneven surface; rubber feet worn | Reposition on a flat surface; replace rubber feet |
| Poor or incomplete mixing      | Speed too low; tube not centered on cup | Increase speed; press tube firmly into center of cup |
| Sample leakage during vortexing | Tube cap not secured; tube overfilled | Cap tightly; reduce fill volume to leave headspace |
| Abnormal noise or grinding     | Cup head loose or damaged; internal bearing wear | Tighten or replace cup head; report to lab manager for service |
| Liquid entered motor housing   | Spill from uncapped tube       | Unplug immediately; wipe and dry thoroughly; do not use until fully dry |
